sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1 (2006)
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF; §§4.2–4.3 and 5.2–5.3, PDF pp. 14–18: perfect-fluid stress, state-function/first-law conventions, and the energy projection of stress conservation.

source_review.read_extent: Read the perfect-fluid tensor in §4.2, the equation-of-state setup and first-law equations (4.10)–(4.14) in §4.3, and the stated rest-frame variables and units.
source_review.supports: The perfect-fluid stress form and the distinction between a supplied relativistic state function and its thermodynamic derivatives, as comparison context for the adopted radiation branch.
source_review.limitations: The notes use particle-number variables and do not supply the entropy-only maps or a_R. The postulate adopts its own state maps and no particle-number current.

contents.name: §§4.2–4.3 Perfect fluid stress-energy tensor and equation of state

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete perfect-fluid divergence calculation (5.4), its parallel energy projection (5.5), and the first-law/Gibbs substitutions through (5.9) in §§5.2–5.3.
source_review.supports: The stress-energy energy projection and its relation to local state differentials, used as independent context for the conditional local entropy-current calculation.
source_review.limitations: The source derives its entropy conclusion using a multicomponent first law and conserved-number currents. The authored proof uses the exact mathematical entropy-only supplier and assumes no number current.

sources.title: Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (2022)
sources.locator: Full 202-page PDF; Chapter XI.2.1, PDF pp. 177–178, equations (XI.17)–(XI.19): zero-conserved-charge ultrarelativistic equation-of-state and temperature scaling.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete Chapter XI.2.1 derivation from the assumed constant pressure/energy-density ratio through equations (XI.17)–(XI.19), including the zero-charge Gibbs–Duhem and fundamental-relation substitutions.
source_review.supports: For an ideal ultrarelativistic gas without conserved charge, the notes state p=epsilon/3 and derive epsilon proportional to T^4 and entropy density proportional to T^3.
source_review.limitations: The result fixes proportionality only, not the positive coefficient a_R. It is a model-context treatment, not a quantum-statistical derivation or measured coefficient.

source_review.read_extent: Read the perfect-fluid stress form in Chapter X.3.1, the entropy-current proof in X.3.2 a through its final contraction, and the zero-charge scaling derivation in XI.2.1.
source_review.supports: Independent context for perfect-fluid stress and entropy-current reasoning, and for the ultrarelativistic relation p=epsilon/3 with the T^4/T^3 scaling.
source_review.limitations: The entropy proof uses a conserved charge and thermodynamic Gibbs identities absent from this entropy-only branch. The local proof is supplied by the mathematics item and is checked directly.

sources.title: N. Andersson and G. L. Comer, Variational multifluid dynamics and causal heat conductivity, arXiv:0908.1707v1 (2009)
sources.locator: Full 15-page PDF; §4, equations (4.2)–(4.14), PDF pp. 5–8: rigid-solid reduction, near-equilibrium linearization, constant-parameter Cattaneo law, and generalized-entropy comparison.

source_review.read_extent: Read §4 from the simplified rigid-solid entropy-momentum equation through the heat-flux form, its near-equilibrium linearization, equations (4.9)–(4.12), and the generalized-entropy comparison through (4.14).
source_review.supports: A variational multifluid treatment of the constant-parameter Cattaneo law as a near-equilibrium rigid-solid model and its relation to an effective quadratic entropy.
source_review.limitations: The authors explicitly treat constant alpha/(sT) as a comparison assumption and discuss its temperature dependence. Their framework does not establish this postulate as a universal material law or supply the local PDE proofs below.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §4 derivation of the linearized constant-parameter relaxation relation and the discussion immediately following equations (4.10)–(4.14).
source_review.supports: Model context for the adopted constitutive relation and effective entropy form.
source_review.limitations: The paper does not prove the exact production identity for this item, the symmetric-system estimates, or the relativistic speed inequality; those are local conditional deductions.

source_review.read_extent: Read the same rigid-solid constant-parameter Cattaneo derivation and its stated near-equilibrium restrictions.
source_review.supports: The effective subsystem solved by the constructed damped mode.
source_review.limitations: The paper does not report this Fourier mode or any measurement; the example is verified by direct substitution.

sources.locator: Full 13-page PDF; §2.1, equations (1)–(3) and surrounding discussion, PDF pp. 1–3: Fourier diffusion, phenomenological Cattaneo relaxation, the telegrapher equation, and causal relativistic context.

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.1 from the energy-balance and Fourier equations through the Cattaneo equation, telegrapher consequence, and the discussion of alternative relativistic formulations.
source_review.supports: An independent relativistic-thermal treatment of finite-relaxation heat conduction and its relation to propagation speed.
source_review.limitations: The paper calls the simple Cattaneo term phenomenological and notes that it is not tied to a clear underlying microphysics. Its full stellar derivation is not imported into the fixed-Minkowski model.

source_review.limitations: The paper does not prove this item's exact coefficient inequality or its symmetric-system evolution statement; those follow from the stated equations and math supplier.
